req.title: Redirect-to supports custom status codes
req.statement: The system shall honour the 'status_code' query parameter on /redirect-to for values 301, 302, 303, 307, and 308.

doc.reasoning: The redirect_to() handler reads 'status_code' from query args, validates it is in [300,400), and sets response.status_code accordingly. To kill mutations we must: (1) assert exact status codes for each valid value (301,302,303,307,308); (2) test the boundary at 300 (inclusive lower bound) and 399 (inclusive upper bound); (3) test 299 and 400 which must NOT change the default 302; (4) verify the Location header is set to the exact url supplied; (5) test missing status_code falls back to 302; (6) test a non-redirect status_code (e.g. 200) is ignored. This covers EP, BVA, DT, NEG heuristics and catches operator-flip mutations (>= vs >, < vs <=), constant mutations (300->301, 400->399), and boolean/branch mutations.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_status_301
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_status_301():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=301', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 301
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_status_301()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact
actions: Iterate over [301,302,303,307,308] and send GET /redirect-to with each status_code
expected: Each response status code matches the requested code exactly
Location header is http://example.com for each
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact():
    for code in [301, 302, 303, 307, 308]:
        r = client.get(
            '/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=' + str(code),
            follow_redirects=False
        )
        assert r.status_code == code, f'Expected {code}, got {r.status_code}'
        assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_boundary_301_vs_300
actions: Send GET /redirect-to with status_code=301 and separately with status_code=300
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_boundary_301_vs_300():
    r301 = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://a.com&status_code=301', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r301.status_code == 301
    assert r301.status_code != 300
    assert r301.status_code != 302
    r300 = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://a.com&status_code=300', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r300.status_code == 300
    assert r300.status_code != 301
    assert r300.status_code != 302

test_redirect_to_boundary_301_vs_300()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_default_is_not_301_or_303
expected: Response status code is exactly 302, not 301, not 303, not 307, not 308
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_default_is_not_301_or_303():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.status_code != 301
    assert r.status_code != 303
    assert r.status_code != 307
    assert r.status_code != 308
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_default_is_not_301_or_303()
